name: Table

hero.title: Edit one cell. One cell updates. No `React.memo`.
hero.lede: TanStack Table v9, with the table's state stored in Pyreon signals. Sort, filter, paginate and group with the API you know; change one price and exactly one text node changes, at 100 rows or 1,000, with no memo comparator to keep correct.

why.title: A data grid without the performance tuning chapter.

items.title: Cell-level updates by default
items.text: An in-place edit re-runs only the edited row's cells (six in a six-column table) and writes one DOM node. With React you get that by memoizing rows on `row.original` and keeping every update immutable; here it is how the adapter works.

items.title: The table's state is signals
items.text: v9's reactivity seam is backed by Pyreon signals, so `table.getRowModel()` read in JSX subscribes like any signal. No `table.Subscribe` wrapper, no selector.

items.title: Options as a function
items.text: `useTable(() => ({ data: products(), columns, features }))` reads signals inside; change `products` and the table re-syncs.

items.title: Correct before clever
items.text: A cell that reads table state (selection, sort) stays right when that state changes. The same cell inside a row memoized on `original` freezes; the adapter re-runs cells on a structure change on purpose.

difference.title: The memo you no longer write.

before.label: React + @tanstack/react-table 9
before.caption: Per-row updates need a memoized row component, a comparator on `row.original`, and immutable edits everywhere.

after.label: with @pyreon/table
after.caption: Keyed rows, reactive cells. Editing one price touches one text node.

comingFrom.title: Same core, same column defs, different render loop.
comingFrom.note: `tableFeatures`, column defs, row models and `sortFn_*` / `filterFn_*` move over unchanged; they come from the same `@tanstack/table-core` v9. The two changes: options become a function, and rows render through keyed `<For>` with `visibleCells` and `flexRenderCell` instead of `.map()`.

demo.title: Sort, filter, edit.
demo.text: 1,000 products. Click a header to sort, type to filter, and double-click a price to edit it. Two counters show what your last edit cost: the cells that re-ran (one row's worth) and the DOM nodes written (one).
demo.spec: 1,000 products × 4 columns (name, category, price, stock) in a `useTable` table with sorting and global filtering, rendered with keyed `<For>` + `visibleCells` + `flexRenderCell`. Header click toggles sorting; the filter input sets the global filter. Double-clicking a price opens an input; Enter or blur writes the new price into the data signal (a new object for that row only). Each cell accessor increments a counter when it runs; a MutationObserver on the tbody counts characterData/childList records. After an edit the two counters show the cells re-run by that edit (4, the edited row) and the DOM writes (1); they update on edits only, not on sort or filter (a sort re-runs every cell by design, see limits).

features.title: Every TanStack feature, plus Pyreon's own pieces.

items.name: `useTable(() => options)`
items.text: Returns the v9 `Table` directly; its state is signals.

items.name: `flexRenderCell` + `visibleCells`
items.text: The fine-grained pair: a cell subscribes to its own row, a row's cell list to column geometry.

items.name: `flexRender`
items.text: Headers and footers from column-def templates: strings, functions or JSX.

items.name: Selection, expanding, pinning
items.text: Row selection, row expanding, row and column pinning.

items.name: `createTableState`
items.text: A dependency-free sort, filter, paginate and select engine for simple tables, and the one that runs natively.

recipes.title: Sort, search and page a product list
recipes.text: Register only what the table uses. Changing the data signal re-syncs; sorting and filtering are the TanStack calls you know.
recipes.code:
const features = tableFeatures({
  rowSortingFeature,
  sortedRowModel: createSortedRowModel(),
  sortFns: { alphanumeric: sortFn_alphanumeric, basic: sortFn_basic },
  columnFilteringFeature,
  globalFilteringFeature,
  filteredRowModel: createFilteredRowModel(),
  filterFns: { includesString: filterFn_includesString },
  rowPaginationFeature,
  paginatedRowModel: createPaginatedRowModel(),
})

const table = useTable(() => ({
  features, data: products(), columns, globalFilterFn: 'includesString',
}))

table.getColumn('price')!.toggleSorting(true) // most expensive first
table.setGlobalFilter('desk')  // ['Standing desk', 'Desk lamp']
table.setGlobalFilter('')
table.setPageSize(2)           // 3 pages of 5 products

recipes.title: A table that also runs on iOS and Android
recipes.text: `createTableState` has no dependencies: sort, filter, paginate and select over your data, rendered with `<For>`.
recipes.code:
import { createTableState } from '@pyreon/table'

const t = createTableState({
  data: products,
  columns: [{ id: 'name' }, { id: 'price' }],
  pageSize: 2,
  rowId: (p) => p.name,
})

t.toggleSort('price')   // asc: Plant pot, Desk lamp
t.toggleSort('price')   // desc: Standing desk, USB-C dock
t.setFilter('desk')     // Standing desk, Desk lamp
t.toggleSelected('Desk lamp')
t.selectedIds()         // ['Desk lamp']

<For each={t.rows()} by={(p) => p.name}>{(p) => <Text>{p.name}</Text>}</For>

api.title: A thin adapter and the whole core.

limits.title: Render rows with `<For>`, not `.map()`
limits.text: A `.map()` over rows rebuilds the whole `<tbody>` on every change. Keyed `<For>` with `visibleCells` and `flexRenderCell` is what makes edits cell-sized.

limits.title: Sorting re-runs every cell
limits.text: A sort or any structure change re-runs all cells (memoized React rows re-run none); DOM writes are the same keyed moves on both sides. That is the price of cells that read table state staying correct.

limits.title: An edit that changes sort order waits
limits.text: Editing a value updates the cell at once, but rows re-position on the next structure or state change. `toggleSorting` and `setSorting` reorder normally.

limits.title: Register features explicitly
limits.text: v9 includes only what you list in `tableFeatures`, which keeps bundles small; build the object once at module scope. `row.getVisibleCells()` needs `columnVisibilityFeature`; without it, `visibleCells` falls back to every cell of the row.

faq.a: In real Chromium, against react-table with memoized rows at 1,000 × 6, two runs: replace 1.11–1.18×, sort 1.09–1.10×, unmount 1.42–1.45× faster; mount and single-cell update tie in one run and are 1.03× ahead in the other, so we do not count them as wins. Under happy-dom (one run) the record shows losses at mount (1,000 rows), single-cell update (1,000) and sort (100); happy-dom is a JavaScript DOM, which is why the headline uses the browser.

faq.q: Do I have to learn a new table API?
faq.a: No. Features, column defs, row models and every table method are TanStack Table v9. Two things change: options become a function, and rows render through keyed `<For>`.

faq.q: How big a table can it handle?
faq.a: It renders every row you give it. For thousands of rows, page them, or render the visible window with `@pyreon/virtual`.
`useTable` stays web. `createTableState` covers the common table (one sort column, a text filter, pages, selection), is plain signals, and lowers to iOS and Android. Native targets are experimental.

benchmarks.p: Same `table-core` on both sides; React rows are memoized on `row.original`, the fair comparison. In the browser Pyreon wins replace, sort and unmount in both runs; mount and single-cell update are a tie in one run and 1.03× ahead in the other. The happy-dom rows at the bottom (one run) time a JavaScript DOM, not a browser; they include three losses, kept here so you can see them.
